reviewer: Another agent in the same session; not organizationally independent.
conclusion: Economic figures and paired-effect claims in the reviewed abstract, result and conclusion agree with independently reconstructed histories. The defensible positive result is conditional prospective adoption value under a seed-inclusive funding policy, not established historical R&D repayment, initial adoption from the stricter earned-funds policy, a second tested capability, or real customer adoption.
materialInterpretationBoundaries: Final fixed-target campaign is post-exploratory and reuses seeds; normal-approximation intervals quantify conditional Monte Carlo variability, not external profitability or independent confirmation.
All earlier primary and exploratory failures remain part of the evidence; the final campaign addresses an identified pricing-heuristic defect and does not delete those outcomes.

All 398 B policy-diagnostic adoptions occur under seed-inclusive eligibility. The earned rule takes min(cash-obligations-reserve, collections-all_accrued_costs-reserve), which requires a fresh USD200 reserve from net earnings in addition to checking liquidity. The resulting no-earned-adoption finding is policy-specific, not a theorem that any use of operating profit is impossible.

Four positive-mean B conditions occur only in the tested adoption-only, zero-integration, higher-arrival, seed-inclusive cells. Those grid coordinates are not universally necessary conditions. Additional unknown costs or plausible behavior outside the tested envelope can reverse them.
Adoption-only excludes historical research; full-history opening expense is a declared scenario allowance, not measured all-in historical cost.
B/C equality is imposed by symmetric modeled policies, information, cost and effects. Finite production parity does not establish equal complete construction efficiency or autonomous invention.
Direct avoided-cost payback is not sufficient for a positive enterprise causal effect: 72 final-diagnostic B paths repay the direct cost measure while B-minus-A is negative.
No second tested productive asset exists. Positive cash or sixteen positive earned-availability endings are not a second capability cycle.
No actual customer collection, token profit, financial transaction or protocol settlement is established.
auditScope: Every studied-enterprise A/B/C invoice, bill, cash event, balance, reserve, investment funding event, canonical projection and published aggregate was reconciled across 19440 histories.

All-provider simulated job identities and finite buyer commitments were checked. Competitor actions and final summaries are exported, but competitor event-by-event invoices/bills/cash arrays are not exported by the frozen core; the independent outcome audit cannot claim complete competitor-event reconciliation. Shared settlement functions and synthetic controls cover their implemented budget rules.
Physical production and its exact replay are reviewed by the production owner; this economic review does not independently reproduce every physical experiment.
editorialCorrectionsSentToParent: Primary construction and adoption grids both use .5/4/16/40 hours, not 12.
Profit is net recognized invoices less accrued costs; after complete collection drain it equals collections less accrued costs.
Reconstruction is a recorded alternative route cost; adopt-existing is selected because it is no more expensive, rather than a learned active construction policy.
Prefer externally anchored or partially calibrated over suggesting exact-task demand and WTP are estimated.
Avoid calling a fixed target independently validated as competent or optimal.
